scenario.summary: The Apex Accelerator campaign uses malicious npm packages and a fake Web3 platform to target cryptocurrency startups with info-stealing malware. The attack chain involves a supply-chain delivery mechanism that fetches platform-specific executables (Bun/Rust) to retrieve and execute further payloads on Windows and macOS, ultimately exfiltrating data via Telegram.

meta.rationale: Focus on engineering and developer workstations where npm is in use. The software inventory scoping step narrows behavior queries to only the affected hosts, reducing telemetry cost.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary targets developer workstations by tricking users into installing malicious npm packages that masquerade as Web3 auditing tools to execute platform-specific backdoors from within the project directory.

hunt.name: Apex Accelerator npm supply-chain delivery
hunt.description: The adversary targets crypto start-ups by distributing backdoored npm packages. The hunt is gated on a software inventory lead to minimize telemetry costs. The hunt identifies these packages in software inventory, then fans out to examine generalized binary execution from within node_modules directories and associated network callbacks. The analyst reviews the correlated evidence to confirm the intrusion.

nodes.label: Detect malicious npm packages and suspicious paths

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version, install_path, vendor_name, provider FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (instr(',' || '{{target_packages}}' || ',', ',' || package_name || ',') > 0 OR LOWER(install_path) LIKE '%\\node_modules\\.apex%' OR LOWER(install_path) LIKE '%/node_modules/.apex%')
config.description: Find hosts where the malicious Apex packages or their hidden configuration directories are present. The query use the instr() pattern because the platform expands the target_packages list as a comma-joined string; this ensures exact matches for each package name within the SQLite engine.
config.expected_signal: Rows identify specific hosts and users that installed the malicious packages. Silence means the specific packages or suspicious .apex directory patterns are not present in current inventory.

primitive_config.label: Detect malicious npm packages and suspicious paths
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version, install_path, vendor_name, provider FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (instr(',' || '{{target_packages}}' || ',', ',' || package_name || ',') > 0 OR LOWER(install_path) LIKE '%\\node_modules\\.apex%' OR LOWER(install_path) LIKE '%/node_modules/.apex%')
primitive_config.expected: Rows identify specific hosts and users that installed the malicious packages. Silence means the specific packages or suspicious .apex directory patterns are not present in current inventory.

config.objective: Decide if the identified hosts show evidence of the malicious Apex npm packages or suspicious local project configurations that requires further behavioral analysis.
config.description: Decide if the findings in the software inventory warrant an expensive investigation into process and network telemetry.
config.expected_signal: A verdict for each host with a malicious package installation.
config.success_criteria: A verdict of suspicious or benign per host.

config.question: the assess-lead verdict is suspicious for at least one host
config.condition: the assess-lead verdict is suspicious for at least one host
config.description: Stop the hunt if no malicious packages were found, preventing expensive queries across the whole estate.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_path, process_cmd_line, user_name, COUNT(*) as runs, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\\node_modules\\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%/node_modules/%') AND (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%.exe' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%.node' OR on_disk = 0 OR (on_disk = 1 AND process_name NOT LIKE '%.%')) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, process_name, process_path, process_cmd_line, user_name
config.description: Identify any executable binary (PE or Mach-O) launched from within a node_modules directory tree. This generalized search captures renamed loaders or supporting components.
config.expected_signal: An executable seen on very few machines launched from a project dependency directory. Fleet-wide presence would suggest a legitimate developer tool.

primitive_config.label: Generalized binary execution from node_modules

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_path, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, COUNT(*) as connections, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_network_connection WHERE (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\\node_modules\\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%/node_modules/%') AND disposition = 'Allowed' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, process_name, process_path, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port
config.description: Identify external network connections initiated by processes running from node_modules. This effectively pivots from the execution leads to find callbacks without relying on a static domain list.
config.expected_signal: Network connections to external IPs from binaries located in node_modules project trees.

config.objective: Evaluate whether the installation of suspicious packages led to binary execution from node_modules and associated C2 communication, indicating a successful supply-chain intrusion.
config.description: Correlate the package installation leads with generalized binary execution and network callbacks into a single verdict per host.
config.expected_signal: A high-confidence verdict citing specific processes and network requests.
config.success_criteria: A verdict of malicious | suspicious | benign per host.

config.question: the triage-findings verdict is malicious for at least one host
config.condition: the triage-findings verdict is malicious for at least one host
config.description: Escalate malicious findings to containment or route suspicious hits for human review.
Stop further command execution and exfiltration by isolating the affected host.
config.instructions: Isolate the host and preserve process memory for the loader binaries and any child shells.

config.description: Review findings and prepare for incident response.
config.instructions: Confirm the presence of the npm package and investigate the child processes of the identified loaders for shell execution. Review any HTTP activity from these processes to identify the specific C2 server and fetched commands.

config.description: Record the results and confirm the absence of these specific packages.
config.instructions: If no hits were found, record that the estate shows no evidence of the Apex Accelerator npm packages or suspicious binary execution from project directories within the lookback window.
